_readme: Labelled CO -> PO competency corpus for GAPC v4.0 (11 POs).
GOLD LABELS ARE JUDGEMENTS, and it matters where they come from. Each
cell is labelled by reading the outcome against the *verbatim* NBA PO
statement, not against what a college happened to publish. Published
articulation matrices were deliberately NOT used as ground truth: the
well-documented failure of real matrices is over-mapping — a CO claiming
eight POs — and training against them would teach the engine to do the
same thing this product exists to prevent.
SCALE. 2 = strong: the outcome's core action is what the PO describes.
1 = partial: the PO is genuinely exercised but incidentally, or at a
lower depth than the PO asks. 0 = no match, and is the default for every
cell not listed — most of the matrix is 0, which is the point.
CONSERVATISM. Where a mapping is arguable it is labelled 1, not 2. A
missed mapping costs a human one click; a spurious level 3 gets bulk-
approved into a SAR and is the failure this engine is calibrated against.
SPLIT. dev is inspected while tuning; holdout is scored and never read.
The AKTU courses are verbatim from the B.Tech ECE (Advanced Communication
Technology) 2026-27 scheme, rewritten only where the published statement
fails the quality test — the mapping engine sees the corrected text.

CO1.statement: Describe the concept of VLSI design and CMOS circuits and delay study.

CO2.statement: Analyze mathematical methods and circuit analysis models in analysis of CMOS digital electronics circuits.

CO3.statement: Design and analyze various combinational and sequential circuits based on CMOS technology.

CO4.statement: Examine power logic circuits and different semiconductor memories used in present day technology.

CO5.statement: Interpret faults in digital circuits, fault models and various testing methodologies.

CO1.statement: Design logic gates using CMOS technology.

CO2.statement: Implement combinational and sequential circuits using CMOS logic.

CO3.statement: Analyze amplifier circuits using simulation tools.

CO4.statement: Design sequential circuits such as flip flops.

CO5.statement: Perform layout design for physical analysis of MOS transistors using modern EDA tools.

CO1.statement: Describe mobile radio and cellular communication fundamentals and their application to propagation mechanisms, path loss models and multi-path phenomenon.

CO2.statement: Analyze the performance of various voice coding and diversity techniques.

CO3.statement: Apply the knowledge of wireless transmission basics to explain the concepts of equalization and multiple access techniques.

CO4.statement: Examine the performance of cellular systems such as GSM, CDMA and LTE using theoretical and mathematical aspects.

CO5.statement: Describe mobile adhoc networks and the existing and upcoming data communication networks in the wireless and mobile communication domain.

CO1.statement: Analyze various parameters and characteristics of the transmission line and waveguide and select waveguide components as per applications.

CO2.statement: Design simple microwave circuits and devices such as couplers, attenuators, phase shifters and isolators.

CO3.statement: Analyze the difference between conventional tubes and microwave tubes for the transmission of electromagnetic waves.

CO4.statement: Measure microwave parameters using standard laboratory instruments and equipment.

CO5.statement: Differentiate different radars and identify applications and uses of their supporting systems.

courses.title: Drone Systems: Design, Control and Navigation

CO1.statement: Explain the constraints and opportunities in UAV miniaturization and aerial networking.

CO2.statement: Represent drone systems using state-space models and apply control theory to analyze their stability.

CO3.statement: Analyze the aerodynamic behaviour and propulsion trade-offs in UAV design and navigation.

CO4.statement: Identify UAV control systems using modern control techniques for both autonomous and semi-autonomous operations.

CO5.statement: Identify the rules and safety practices for drone operation in India and globally, including licensing, geofencing and traffic management.

CO1.statement: Explain the evolution of wireless communication systems and the requirements of 5G technology.

CO2.statement: Explain the architecture and key components of 5G networks, including core and radio access networks.

CO3.statement: Analyze the features of 5G new radio, including protocol stack, frame structure and resource allocation.

CO4.statement: Evaluate the performance of key enabling technologies such as massive MIMO, beamforming and mmWave communication.

CO5.statement: Examine the applications, performance metrics and deployment challenges associated with modern 5G wireless communication systems.

CO1.statement: Explain the architecture of a database management system and the relational data model.

CO2.statement: Apply entity-relationship modelling to design a normalized relational schema for a given application.

CO3.statement: Construct SQL queries to retrieve and manipulate data from a relational database.

CO4.statement: Analyze transaction schedules for serializability and recoverability.

CO5.statement: Evaluate concurrency control and recovery techniques for a given workload.

courses.title: Major Project
courses.source: seed catalogue — the professional-skill POs, which content courses never exercise

CO1.statement: Identify a complex engineering problem and survey the current research literature relevant to it.

CO2.statement: Design and develop a solution using appropriate modern engineering tools.

CO3.statement: Evaluate the solution against societal, environmental, safety and whole-life cost considerations.

CO4.statement: Demonstrate effective teamwork and manage the project schedule and cost within stated constraints.

CO5.statement: Communicate the work through an effective technical report and presentation.

courses.title: Environmental Engineering
courses.source: seed catalogue — exercises PO6 and PO7, which most courses do not

CO1.statement: Explain the structure of ecosystems and the impact of engineering activity on biodiversity.

CO2.statement: Analyze sources and effects of water and air pollution on public health and the environment.

CO3.statement: Evaluate solid waste management practices against sustainability and whole-life cost criteria.

CO4.statement: Apply environmental legislation and ethical principles to engineering practice.

courses.title: Engineering Thermodynamics
courses.source: seed catalogue — a pure-fundamentals course, so most POs must stay 0

CO1.statement: Explain the fundamental concepts and laws of thermodynamics.

CO2.statement: Apply the first law of thermodynamics to closed and open systems.

CO3.statement: Analyze thermodynamic processes using the second law and entropy principles.

CO4.statement: Evaluate the performance of power and refrigeration cycles.
